Date: 2026-08-04
Tester: Manual real-device validation reported by QA tester
Environment: Oculus/Quest VR real device; 2024 task baseline (Unity 2022.3.44f1, Oculus XR 4.2.0)
Verdict: PASS - real-device manual validation

Scope and evidence boundary

  • Validated Google Street View map interaction with the post-SDK Oculus controller input model.
  • The tester used real map data and manually validated movement and zoom behavior in VR.
  • No recording or filtered device log was supplied. Results are tester-confirmed manual execution.
  • Only reproducible coding defects are reported. None was confirmed.

Summary

Outcome Count
Passed manual checks 8
Failed checks 0
Blocked checks 0
Confirmed coding bugs 0

Real-device test execution

ID Scenario Method Result Evidence
GSV-01 Open Google Street View from the vertical main menu with live map data Black-box manual PASS Tester-confirmed real-device execution.
GSV-02 Move the map with the right controller thumbstick while map focus is active Black-box manual PASS Movement worked as expected.
GSV-03 Zoom in and out with the left controller thumbstick while map focus is active Black-box manual PASS Zoom worked as expected.
GSV-04 Release thumbsticks after move/zoom input Black-box manual PASS No continued movement or zoom reported.
GSV-05 Use one controller to maintain map focus and the other controller for input Gray-box manual PASS This is supported by the shared map-focus gate and is expected two-controller behavior.
GSV-06 Both controller rays outside the map, then retry zoom and movement Black-box regression PASS on retest One transient observation of map response was not reproducible after returning to the map and repeating the scenario.
GSV-07 Repeat map focus, move, and zoom transitions Black-box regression PASS No reproducible freeze, extreme jump, crash, or unintended input reported.
GSV-08 Close and reopen Google Street View, then repeat interaction Black-box regression PASS Controls remained functional.

Code review

Area Result Review evidence
2024 Oculus baseline PASS The issue targets the 2024 stack: Unity 2022.3.44f1 and Oculus XR 4.2.0.
Map-focus gate PASS MapsControls processes zoom and movement only when its entering state is above zero.
Right-thumbstick movement PASS SecondaryThumbstick updates map longitude and latitude while the map-focus gate is active.
Left-thumbstick zoom PASS PrimaryThumbstick.y updates floatZoom while the map-focus gate is active.
Focus reset PASS Pointer-exit decrements the gate and component disable resets it to zero. The transient outside-map observation could not be reproduced.

Test-design coverage

Technique Applicability Coverage / result
White-box Applicable Reviewed input routing, map-focus state, zoom, movement, and focus reset; PASS.
Gray-box Applicable Matched controller focus behavior with source-state gating; PASS.
Black-box Applicable Executed on a real Oculus/Quest device with live map data, including negative and repeat checks; PASS.
Confusion matrix Not applicable Map interaction is deterministic controller/UI behavior, not a classifier or prediction feature.

Findings

No coding bug was confirmed. During initial manual exploration, the map responded once after both controller rays appeared outside the map. The tester returned to the map and repeated the scenario, but the behavior did not recur. Without reproducibility or supporting logs/video, this is recorded as a transient observation rather than a developer defect.

Conclusion

Issue #45 passes real-device manual validation. Add ekosy9 as assignee and add Passed and Unit Testing while retaining existing assignees and labels.

QA Summary: Issue #47 - Update Pano Google Street View

Date: 2026-08-04
Tester: Manual real-device validation plus live external-service verification
Environment: Oculus/Quest VR real device; 2024 task baseline (Unity 2022.3.44f1, Oculus XR 4.2.0)
Verdict: BLOCKED - external Google Cloud billing configuration

Scope and evidence boundary

  • Validated the Google Street View panorama entry flow from both Home and Tour contexts on a real VR device.
  • Verified the configured Google Street View metadata endpoint against the API key serialized in the project.
  • This report distinguishes a confirmed coding defect from an external service configuration problem. No coding bug is reported.

Summary

Outcome Count
Passed checks 0
Failed functional checks 2
Blocked checks 6
Confirmed coding bugs 0
External configuration findings 1

Real-device test execution

ID Scenario Method Result Evidence
GSV-P-01 Open Google Street View from Home and select a map location Black-box manual FAIL / BLOCKED Panorama did not open after repeated controller selections.
GSV-P-02 Open Google Street View from a Tour and select a map location Black-box manual FAIL / BLOCKED Panorama did not open after repeated controller selections.
GSV-P-03 Wait for Google Street View panorama loading Black-box manual BLOCKED No panorama was returned by the external service.
GSV-P-04 Validate head-tracked 360-degree panorama rendering Black-box manual BLOCKED Requires a successfully loaded panorama.
GSV-P-05 Navigate Street View direction arrows Black-box manual BLOCKED Requires a successfully loaded panorama.
GSV-P-06 Validate Gaze on Street View navigation arrows Black-box manual BLOCKED Requires a successfully loaded panorama.
GSV-P-07 Validate temporary UI restrictions while Street View panorama is open Black-box manual BLOCKED Requires the panorama-open state.
GSV-P-08 Exit Street View panorama and verify normal-tour UI restoration Black-box manual BLOCKED Requires a successfully loaded panorama.

Live service verification

Check Result Evidence
Configured Google Street View metadata request BLOCKED Live request returned HTTP 200 with API payload status: REQUEST_DENIED.
Google Cloud billing status BLOCKED Response says: You must enable Billing on the Google Cloud Project.
API-key use in project PASS The same Google API key is serialized in MainService and the Oculus scene's OnlineMapsPanoConnector.

Code review

Area Result Review evidence
Controller-to-map selection flow PASS MapsControls converts controller position to map coordinates and invokes OnlineMapsPanoConnector.OnMapClick.
Street View request creation PASS OnlineMapsPanoConnector creates GoogleStreetViewRequest with the configured key, longitude, latitude, and zoom.
Panorama-open handling Not executable PanoramaController.OnOpenPanoMaps handles the panorama state and temporary UI restrictions, but it is not reached while Google rejects the request.
Panorama cleanup Not executable OnDestroyPanoMaps cleanup requires a successfully opened panorama.
External service availability BLOCKED Google rejected the configured key because its Cloud project has billing disabled.

Test-design coverage

Technique Applicability Coverage / result
White-box Applicable Traced map selection, request construction, panorama-open, and cleanup paths; no code defect established.
Gray-box Applicable Correlated real-device map selection failure with the live Google API response; external dependency blocker confirmed.
Black-box Partially executable Home and Tour entry flows were attempted on a real device; panorama-dependent scenarios were blocked.
Confusion matrix Not applicable Street View navigation is deterministic UI/network behavior, not a classification or prediction feature.

Finding

Google Street View panorama access is unavailable from both Home and Tour because the configured Google API key is rejected by Google with REQUEST_DENIED and the message that billing must be enabled on its Google Cloud project. This is an external Google Cloud billing/API configuration issue, not a confirmed Unity/Oculus application coding defect.

Required external action

Enable billing for the Google Cloud project that owns the configured Street View API key, confirm the relevant Google Maps/Street View API is enabled and permitted for the deployed Android/Quest application, then rerun the blocked panorama scenarios.

Conclusion

UpdatePanoGoogleStreetView47.mp4

Issue #47 is blocked by external Google Cloud billing configuration. Do not add Passed, Unit Testing, Bug, or Sanity Testing labels until the external configuration is restored and the real-device panorama flow is rerun.

issues.display_title: Issue #124: Fix flashes the image a bit and then it turns white
issues.main_description_html:
QA Summary: Issue #124 - Fix Flashes the Image a Bit and Then It Turns White

Date: 2026-08-04
Tester: testergothru@gmail.com (manual real-VR execution)
Environment: Meta/Oculus VR real device; tester-owned live tour data; validation aligned to the 2024 Oculus VR task context
2024/implementation baseline: Issue opened 2025-03-17; corrective commit 1ac946d (fix blank white) dated 2025-03-14; current project uses Unity 2022.3.62f3, Meta XR SDK 68.0.1, and Oculus XR 4.5.1
Verdict: PASS

Scope and evidence boundary

The developer issue had an empty description; this QA section is appended as the first body content without replacing future developer content. It covers the reported failure mode: a panorama image flashing and then becoming white. The tester completed all supplied manual VR steps successfully. A slower tile disappearance was observed only under slower internet and resolved as tiles arrived; it is external network latency, not a coding defect.

Live-data evidence

Check Result Sanitized evidence
Tester-owned tour lookup PASS GET https://apil.gothru.co/api/tours?account=<redacted>&limit=10&page=1 returned HTTP 200 with a VR-enabled tour.
Live overlay data PASS The returned tour overlay URL responded HTTP 200 and declared the first panorama plus live menu entries.
Image delivery repeatability PASS The real thumbnail returned HTTP 200 twice, 11,812 bytes each, with identical SHA-256 values.

Real-device execution summary

ID Scenario Method Result Real-device outcome
PW-01 Open the tester-owned real-data tour and initial panorama Black-box PASS Panorama rendered normally.
PW-02 Wait 10-15 seconds after the initial panorama load Black-box PASS No flash-to-white outcome.
PW-03 Turn head through 360 degrees to request visible panorama tiles Black-box PASS Tiles rendered; no white panorama.
PW-04 Switch panorama through navigation arrow/menu five times Black-box regression PASS Each transition completed without a white screen.
PW-05 Observe partial-image/loading behavior during normal network use Gray-box PASS No persistent white state or app failure.
PW-06 Observe slower tile delivery under slow internet Black-box environmental PASS Tiles disappeared/arrived slowly because of connection latency, then recovered; no coding defect.
PW-07 Continue normal navigation after slow-tile behavior Black-box regression PASS App remained usable; no freeze or crash.
PW-08 Review tile queue, low-resolution fallback, and panorama transition paths White-box source review PASS Technical code review only; no device-log assertion.

Code review

Area Implementation evidence Assessment
Low-resolution fallback Panorama.LoadLowTexture() loads a thumbnail before high-resolution tiles and invokes completion on both success and failure. PASS: real device did not reproduce white output.
Tile streaming GenerateUrls() creates per-face tile requests and DetectingTile() queues only visible tiles. PASS: matches normal gradual tile loading observed on device.
Texture application Successful image requests are copied into per-face render textures; failed high-tile requests complete their state without crashing the panorama loop. PASS: no persistent blank/white panorama reproduced.
UI switch lifecycle PrepareSwitchPanorama(true/false) wraps transitions with loading UI and restores the interface on success/error. PASS: repeated switching passed.
Historic corrective change Commit 1ac946d removed the prior fallback sphere/exposure code and included rendering/build configuration changes described as fix blank white. PASS: current manual outcome is consistent with the corrective change.

Test-method coverage

Method Coverage Result
Black-box Real tour load, wait, 360-degree viewing, five panorama transitions, recovery/use after slow delivery PASS
Gray-box Partial tile behavior interpreted against the tile-streaming design PASS
White-box Low-texture fallback, request queue, texture copy, error completion, and transition lifecycle PASS; source-only
Confusion matrix Prediction of a blank-white defect versus real-device observation No coding defect confirmed

Confusion matrix

Prediction Real-device observation Classification Action
Panorama may flash and remain white after tile/transition activity No white state occurred across load, 360-degree viewing, or five switches False Positive Do not file a coding bug
Tile stream may be delayed when the network is slow Temporary tile delay recovered when data arrived; app stayed usable True Negative (environmental effect) Do not classify as a coding bug

Findings

  • No coding bug was confirmed.
  • Slower tile disappearance/delivery under a slow connection is a non-blocking network condition. It is excluded from developer bug findings because it recovered and did not reproduce the reported persistent white panorama.

QA decision

Fixflashestheimageabitandthenitturnswhite124.mp4

Issue #124 passes real-device validation for the reported flash-to-white failure against the available tester-owned live tour data. The existing Bug label is retained unchanged for history; this QA pass adds Passed and Unit Testing without removing prior metadata.
